# The Energy Crisis, World War III & the Future of Power with Doomberg

First listed: 2026-10-28 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: The Energy Crisis, World War III & the Future of Power with Doomberg](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-energy-crisis-world-war-iii-and) - 2026-10-28

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Doomberg explains diesel scarcity through refinery and trade bottlenecks, advances a broad World War III and Western-retrenchment thesis, and favors gas midstream infrastructure over refiners. Eisman challenges crude pricing, Russian military performance and Chinese leadership, while predicting no Trump strategic retreat. Primary energy data supports product-market stress but qualifies several quantities and price claims. Russia's claimed rare-earth production rank is contradicted by USGS. Most military-intent and capability assertions lack inspected primary corroboration; they remain guest claims, not Eisman endorsements.

Useful product-versus-crude distinction is mixed with highly confident geopolitical explanations. Quantitative errors, unverified causal assertions and genuine future horizons are kept separate. No overall episode accuracy percentage is appropriate.

## Material claims

<a id="substack-222065451-c001"></a>
### 001. Wars and attacks on energy infrastructure have produced chronic global energy undersupply, making geopolitical resolution the dominant market driver.

**Mixed** | Doomberg | explanation | major

[Source at 3:41-4:58](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-energy-crisis-world-war-iii-and) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Primary inventory and product-supply data support shortages; dominance across all energy markets is broader than the evidence.

Qualification: No specified end date.

Assessment test: Compare supply-demand balances, inventory draws and identified wartime outages.

- [Oil Market Report, October 2026](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-october-2026) (2026-10-14): Oil stocks fell 509 million barrels from end-February. September diesel exports were 700 kb/d lower year over year. Diesel benchmarks exceeded $200, with highs around $220 in Europe and the US. European diesel cracks fell from $100 to about $60 by early October. Global seaborne net gasoil/diesel exports averaged 4.7 mb/d in the first nine months. G7 committed October 2 to accelerate reserve delivery.

<a id="substack-222065451-c004"></a>
### 004. Destroying refineries removes crude buyers and can depress crude prices while raising the price of refined products.

**Right** | Doomberg | explanation | major

[Source at 6:26-6:54](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-energy-crisis-world-war-iii-and) | Stance: conditional | Horizon: not stated

Conditional supply-demand mechanism follows if crude production and end-product demand are held fixed; actual net effects require empirical attribution.

Qualification: Ceteris paribus mechanism; the thought experiment about all refineries and negative prices is more extreme.

Conditional reasoning: With demand for final products unchanged, less refining capacity lowers product supply. With crude supply fixed, less capacity reduces derived demand for crude. This gives opposing directional pressures, not an unconditional net price forecast.

Assessment test: Hold other conditions fixed and model less refinery demand for crude alongside lower product output.

- [Refining crude oil: inputs and outputs](https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/oil-and-petroleum-products/refining-crude-oil-inputs-and-outputs.php) (None): Crude properties and refinery processing determine outputs; light crude can yield gasoline, diesel and jet fuel through simple distillation.

<a id="substack-222065451-c011"></a>
### 011. The Russian diesel loss should be compared with internationally traded diesel, rather than total global oil production.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | supporting

[Source at 12:01-12:07](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-energy-crisis-world-war-iii-and) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Conditional denominator choice is correct for assessing direct traded-diesel exposure, assuming comparable units and market definitions.

Qualification: Endorses the denominator logic, not independent verification of all supplied quantities.

Conditional reasoning: A product-specific supply loss divided by the available traded quantity measures exposure in that product market; dividing by all crude combines non-substitutable outputs. This validates the denominator principle, not the numerical input.

Assessment test: Match the disrupted product and market denominator.
